questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I have a dog and a cow. / A dog is black / but the cow is / black and white.

options.text: I have a dog and a cow

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'A dog is black'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The segment that contains a grammatical error is**: A dog is black**.
 
• In the given sentence, "I have a dog and a cow," both "dog" and "cow" are introduced as specific entities.
 
• When referring back to these specific entities later in the sentence, the correct article should be used.
 
• "A dog is black" suggests any dog, not the specific dog mentioned earlier.
 
• The correct form should be "The dog is black," to appropriately reference the specific dog already mentioned.
 
• Article 'the' is used to refer to a specific noun that is known to the reader or listener, previously mentioned.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** Option 1. **

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

We feed the horse oats for a week because it had eaten all the hay.

options.text: it had eaten all the hay

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'We feed the horse oats'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Original sentence:* "**We feed the horse oats **for a week because it had eaten all the hay."* The error is in the phrase **"We feed the horse oats."** This phrase uses the present tense "**feed**" instead of the past tense "**fed**."
 
• When we say *"We fed the horse oats,"* we are indicating that **the action of feeding the horse oats already occurred in the past.** This matches the context of the sentence, which **discusses actions that have already happened ("it had eaten all the hay").**
 
• **Here's the corrected sentence:**__ *"**We fed the horse oats** for a week because it had eaten all the hay."*
 
• Explanation:

 
 
• **"We fed"** is in the **past tense, **indicating that the action of feeding the horse oats occurred in the past.
 
• **"For a week" **specifies the duration of time during which the feeding occurred.
 
• **"Because it had eaten all the hay"** provides the reason for feeding the horse oats. 
 
 
 
• Imagine a scenario where you have a horse that accidentally eats all its hay before its usual feeding time. You then decide to feed it oats instead for the rest of the week. In this case, you would say,* "**We fed the horse oats** for a week because it had eaten all the hay."*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My apartment / in Delhi / is situated / on second floor.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4. "on second floor".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The segment **"on second floor"** is missing the definite article "**the**" before "second floor."
 
• In English, when referring to floors within a building, the definite article "the" is used, e.g., "the first floor," "the second floor."
 
• The **correct **phrase should be **"on the second floor."**

Therefore, the correct sentence is- *My apartment in Delhi is situated on the second floor.*

questions.question: **Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.**

options.text: There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and a Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: an Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and an Fiat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article is: There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.
 
• Explanation:
 
• The indefinite article "**a**" is used before words that begin with **a consonant sound, while "an" **is used before words that begin with** a vowel sound.**
 
 
• In this sentence, **"Mercedes," "Jaguar," and "Fiat"** all start with consonant sounds, so the correct indefinite article to use is "**a**" before each of them.
 
• **Option 1 **uses "**an" before "Jaguar," **which is incorrect because "**Jaguar**" begins with a consonant sound.
 
• **Option 2** uses **"an" before "Mercedes,"** which is incorrect because "**Mercedes**" begins with a consonant sound.
 
• **Option 4 **uses **"an" before both "Jaguar"** and "**Fiat**," which is incorrect because both words begin with consonant sounds.

questions.question:

Gautam ______all the documents by the time his senior advocate reached the court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence implies that the action of examining the documents was completed before the senior advocate reached the court.
 
• To indicate that an action was completed before another action in the** past**, the** past perfect tense** is used.
 
• Among the given options, the past perfect tense form "**had examined"** is the most appropriate.

Hence, the correct statement is 'Gautam **had examined **all the documents by the time his senior advocate reached the court.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, the past perfect tense is used to describe an action that was completed before another action took place in the past.
 
• The structure of the past perfect tense is:** subject + had + past participle of the verb.**
 
• Using the correct tense is crucial for conveying the intended meaning and the sequence of events accurately.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

If I go to Bangalore, I ______with my nephew.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a **first conditional sentence, **which describes a **probable future event and its result.**
 
• In** first conditional sentences, **the structure is
 
 
• ** *if + present simple + will + base form of the verb*.**
 
 
 
• We use the present simple tense in the **if-clause (If I go) and "will" plus the base form of the verb in the main clause (I will stay).**

Hence, the correct statement is '***If I go to Bangalore, I will stay__ with my nephew.**'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The first conditional is used to talk about** real or possible future situations** and thei**r likely outcomes.**
 
• Other structures fit different types of conditionals: second conditional uses **"if + past simple, would + base form"** for **hypothetical situations**
 
• Third conditional uses **"if + past perfect, would have + past participle"** for **hypothetical situations in the past.**

He felt like a fish out of water as he was not __accustomed for__ living in a large city.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The correct preposition to use with 'accustomed' is 'to'.
 
• Therefore, the phrase 'accustomed to' should be used in place of 'accustomed for'.
 
• Example: He felt like a fish out of water as he was not accustomed to living in a large city.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*****He felt like a fish out of water as he was not accustomed to living in a larg**e city*.'

Hence, the correct statement is '***We were grateful for ____the book __they gave us.'***

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The small coffee shop at the end of the road is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The small coffee shop at the end of the road is being referred to as something belonging to the** speaker,** which is why '**mine' **is the appropriate **possessive** **pronoun.**
 
• Using '**mine' **correctly indicates ownership by the speaker without needing to repeat the noun '**coffee shop'.**
 
• Other options like** 'their', 'my', or 'our' do not **fit grammatically in this context. As these are object pronoun and possessive adjective.

Hence, the correct statement is '***The small coffee shop at the end of the road is mine*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Possessive pronouns **are used to show ownership and do not require an additional noun after them.
 
• Common possessive pronouns include: **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.**
 
• Example:
 
 
• *This book is** mine.***
 
• *Is this pen** yours?***

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

One of their freighters, / a Neptune, / will be leaving/ in two weeks.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: '**a Neptune'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the given sentence is the use of the article **'a'** before **'Neptune'.**
 
• The definite article **'the'** should be used because we are referring to a specific freighter named **'the Neptune'**.
 
 
• **Corrected Sentence:** *“One of their freighters, **the Neptune**, will be leaving in two weeks.”*
 
 
 
• The indefinite article **'a'** is not appropriate in this context.
 
• Hence, **'a Neptune'** is the erroneous part.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article **'the'** is used before a noun when it refers to something **specific** or **previously mentioned.**

 
 
• Example: "I'm reading **the** book I bought yesterday."
 
• Example: "I saw a dog. **The** dog had a friendly face."
